privacy_why_anon_body: Reports are linked to a private device ID that we cannot trace back to you. No phone number, no email, no login needed. You can use the app forever without revealing who you are.
privacy_why_offline_body: The app works in low-connectivity zones. Reports queue locally on your device and upload automatically once the network is back. You never lose what you've captured.
privacy_why_blur_body: Faces are detected and blurred on your phone before the photo is uploaded. The server never sees an unredacted face. This is a UNDP requirement (§2.9) and a CRISP guarantee.

help_sheet_point_2: Reports work offline. They send automatically when you're back online.
help_sheet_point_3: Prefer a different channel? Use WhatsApp, Telegram, SMS, or Voice — same report shape.
help_sheet_point_4: CRISP is open source. Code at github.com/Pratik-Shukla-PY/crisp-platform
privacy_sheet_point_5: Reports are kept only while the crisis response needs them; deleted reports are permanently removed within 24 hours.
privacy_sheet_point_6: Categories of recipients: crisis responders, UNDP analysts, AI verification (Anthropic), encrypted storage (AWS), maps (OSM/Mapbox), messaging (Telegram/WhatsApp/Twilio for SMS+IVR). Data may be processed in countries other than yours.
privacy_sheet_point_7: Your rights: access, correction, deletion, objection, restriction. Contact privacy@crisplabs.tech for any privacy concern.
privacy_rights_6: Request correction: a report's classification or text can be amended by deleting and resubmitting (we'll surface in-place edit shortly).
privacy_rights_7: Object to / restrict processing of a specific report by emailing the contact at the bottom of this page.
privacy_rights_8: Withdraw consent at any time. Withdrawal triggers deletion of all your reports.
privacy_basis_body: We process your reports on the basis of your consent, given when you first tap "Accept & continue" on the home screen. You may withdraw consent at any time by deleting your data; we will not retain reports after withdrawal.
privacy_recipients_lede: CRISP shares your reports only with the categories of recipients listed below, all under contractual or commercial data-protection terms. Data may be processed in countries other than yours.
privacy_recipients_1: Crisis responders & UNDP analysts — to triage and act on the report.
privacy_recipients_2: AI verification (Anthropic Claude) — multi-modal truth-scoring of your photo against satellite imagery; processed in the US.
privacy_recipients_3: Encrypted storage (AWS S3) — region per deployment; default ap-south-1 (India) for UNDP submissions, with server-side encryption at rest.
privacy_recipients_4: Maps & building footprints (OpenStreetMap / Mapbox) — to render the location picker; only the bounding box of your area is shared.
privacy_recipients_5: Messaging gateways (Twilio for SMS / IVR; Telegram & WhatsApp for chat ingestion) — only if you report through those channels.
privacy_recipients_6: Satellite imagery providers (ESA Sentinel-2, Microsoft Planetary Computer, ESA Copernicus) — receive only the bounding box around the reported location, never your photo or device code.
privacy_retention_title: How long we keep your data
privacy_retention_body: Reports are kept only for as long as the active crisis response requires (default retention is indefinite while the crisis is open; analyst review may close a report sooner). When you request deletion, your reports are queued for hard-delete and permanently removed within 24 hours. Photos and audio attached to deleted reports are erased on the same schedule. Anonymous aggregate statistics (counts, regional totals) may be retained as non-personal data after deletion — these never identify you.
privacy_vulnerable_body: CRISP is designed for adult reporters. Children under 16 should report through a trusted adult, parent, or community responder. We take particular care in the processing of personal data of vulnerable categories (people in displacement, marginalised groups, victims of violence) — the same anonymous device-code model applies, and we will never publish identifying details. If you are reporting on behalf of someone vulnerable, the same protections apply.
privacy_contact_body: For any privacy question — access, correction, restriction, objection, or a privacy concern — email privacy@crisplabs.tech. We respond within a reasonable time. For suspected data breaches please email breach@crisplabs.tech. If you are not satisfied with our response, you may further contact the UNDP Chief Data Officer through the UNDP transparency portal at undp.org.
